thread.title: Grand Ledge, Oneida fire station bond on May 5 ballot - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Grand Ledge, Oneida fire station bond on May 5 ballot - NewsBreak

author: Shajaka Shelton
title: Grand Ledge, Oneida fire station bond on May 5 ballot - NewsBreak
text:
By Shajaka Shelton ,
8 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — In the upcoming May 5 election, voters in Grand Ledge and Oneida Township will cast their ballots on a bond proposal that the Grand Ledge Area Emergency Services Authority (GLAESA) says would be used to fund new fire facilities and the purchase of firefighting equipment.
The authority says the proposal comes after a recent facility assessment on the more than 70-year-old fire station and its three-decade-old renovations identified a slew of issues with the building, including “significant issues with the building envelope,” lack of movement joints and drainage system, doors and windows in need of replacement, and more.
“This proposal is the result of long-range planning for the future of emergency services in our community,” said Mike Roman, Chief of the Grand Ledge Fire Department. “Our goal is to ensure our personnel have facilities that support safe, effective, and reliable service for the people we serve.”
The bond proposal would authorize up to $22.59 million in bonds to fund the construction of a new main fire station on Hartel Road near the border between the two municipalities, as well as a smaller substation at or near the current fire station in the city of Grand Ledge, and additional improvements.
GLAESA says the bond would be repaid over 20 years through an estimated levy of 3.04 mills and provided an estimated millage calculator for residents to get a feel for how much the proposal would cost them.
“The proposed project is intended to address facility needs related to personnel space, apparatus access, equipment storage, and day-to-day emergency service operations,” wrote GLAESA in a news release. “The current facility is over 70 years old and simply isn’t meeting the needs of the community and 21st Century Fire Response.”
GLAESA has been planning on building a station on Hartel Road for years now, having purchased property in the area more than twenty years ago. The authority says the current fire station location in downtown Grand Ledge is unsuitable for a new large station.
“This was decided for two reasons: First, to ensure that there is adequate EMT and fire protection on both sides of the bridge in the event of a real tragedy should something ever occur to the bridge, road closure or other situation,” GLAESA said. “Secondly, board members felt that it was important to keep a small sub-station near the most populated area of the district, while still ensuring that our first responders have the facilities and equipment necessary to keep Grand Ledge and Oneida Township safe.”
